schema.title: IUIDocument
schema.description: The project-defined iui/1 wire contract. Semantic validation additionally enforces safe expressions, data and URLs. Native nodes are recognized but unsupported by the portable renderer.

contracts.text:
## 状态与表达式

`state` 保存字符串、有限数值或布尔值。引用写作 `{ "$": "gain" }`，计算写作 `{ "op": "mul", "args": [12, { "$": "gain" }] }`。

可用操作符：`add`、`sub`、`mul`、`div`、`max`、`min`、`round`、`abs`、`clamp`、`gt`、`lt`、`eq`、`if`、`format`。它们是受约束的数据树，不是 JavaScript 源码。未知引用、循环依赖、非法参数、除零及非有限结果会被拒绝。

需要直接求值时，可从主入口导入 `evaluateValue` 和 `evaluateState`；通常由控件与渲染器自动处理即可。

# API and security model

`iui/1` is data, never executable source. Content text is inserted through text nodes. The only HTML sink is KaTeX's generated visual HTML plus accessible MathML with `trust:false`, bounded expansion/size, and strict parsing; model HTML never enters that sink directly. Unsupported TeX falls back to visible source.

## Validation

The JSON Schema is generated from `scripts/generate-schema.mjs`. TypeScript declarations and the Ajv standalone validator are generated in the same step. CI rejects drift. Browser code imports the already generated validator, avoiding runtime `new Function` and allowing a script hash CSP without `unsafe-eval`.

`validateDocument(input)` returns `{ok:true,document}` or `{ok:false,issues}`. It accepts plain JSON values only; custom prototypes, accessors, cyclic objects, reserved keys, nonfinite numbers, and excessive values/text/depth are rejected before Ajv traversal. Semantics additionally reject unknown references, computed cycles, bad operator arities/types, numerical errors, duplicate IDs, unknown state bindings, broken topology endpoints, malformed table widths, invalid chart data, and unsafe resource declarations.

`evaluateValue(value,state,computed)` evaluates a constrained expression and throws on invalid input. `evaluateState(document,override)` returns validated, frozen state/computed results or issues. Controller state updates use this checked path. Numeric operators do not coerce strings. `if` is lazy at evaluation but both branches are inspected for references and types; runtime arithmetic errors still reject the state transition.

Limits include 64 JSON nesting levels, 2,000 node-like objects, 50,000 values, a two-million-UTF-16-code-unit text budget (including JSON keys, retained across merged state updates), and schema-specific row/series/child limits. These limits reduce resource exhaustion; they are not a promise of fixed latency for every valid document.

## Browser boundary

No raw HTML, CSS, JS, callback, import, network action, form submission, or arbitrary AppBlock is accepted. SVG uses a fixed shape list and numeric/color/geometry attribute allowlists. `native` is recognized solely to report `UNSUPPORTED_NATIVE`. It does not load an adapter.

Model URLs are limited to the documented link/image policy. Remote images require a reader action and use no-referrer. URLs still lead to third parties when a reader activates them; validation does not certify the destination's content or privacy. Callers handling confidential documents should avoid remote URLs altogether.

Compiled inline HTML applies a CSP containing the exact SHA-256 of its runtime. It blocks network connections, objects, forms, base URL changes, and remote scripts/fonts; font-src data: permits the bundled official WOFF2 fonts. Styles allow inline rules because the renderer writes bounded, host-owned numeric/enum properties. The host browser's CSP remains authoritative for `mount`; pass `styles:false` and serve the stylesheet when embedding under a stricter host policy.

`compileHtml(input,{assets:'inline',backend:'portable',lang})` emits one self-contained HTML file. `compileArtifact(input,{assets:'shared',assetBase:'./iui-assets/',lang})` also returns an asset map with safe relative file paths. Shared output is intended for a static HTTP server; no claim is made for every browser's file-origin shared-script policy. Both reject unsupported backends.

## Lifecycle and scope

Controllers isolate state. `update` validates the complete next document and resets state. `setState` merges a scalar patch, verifies all bindings and derived values, then updates existing nodes without replacing focused controls. `dispose` is idempotent and removes its owned elements, listeners, and resize observer. External DOM edits by the embedding host are outside this contract.

The library does not authenticate users, persist documents, store credentials, run simulations as scientific truth, fetch sources, or verify model-generated facts. Applications remain responsible for provenance, permissions, and their host threat model.

JSON Schema string `maxLength` and evaluated Value/state string maxima use Unicode code points. A Value string accepts at most 12,000 code points, including astral characters, while the independent whole-document resource budget still counts UTF-16 storage units. The resolved evaluation context (state, computed scalars and the evaluated Value) is checked against the same storage budget before DOM creation or refresh; accepted documents therefore do not defer that rejection until rendering. Native form minLength/maxLength constraints retain HTML UTF-16 semantics; they do not redefine the global string contract.

# Supplied automation views

Three independently implemented finite views: `display-automation`, `list-automations`, and `automation-plan-summary`. They display authored data. They do not create, list, edit or cancel real scheduled tasks, resolve accounts, fetch data, navigate, log impressions or infer schedule/time-zone meaning.

## Data and visible behavior

All accept a nonblank accessible `label`, optional `id`, `disabled`, and `status` (`resolved` by default, `pending`, `failed`). Pending renders an accessible loading block. Failed renders supplied `fallback`, or hides the component. Unresolved records cannot contain active item/step data.

- Display: `item` has `id`, `title`, `scheduleLabel`, safe `url`, optional `emoji` and `disabled`. One full-width task card presents those exact strings.
- List: `headerLabel`, `emptyLabel`, finite `items` (maximum 100), optional `viewAll: {label,url}`. Shows the first five items; the footer is a supplied local intent, not a loaded second page. Empty lists display `emptyLabel`.
- Plan: `title`, `goalLabel`, `steps` and `statusLabels` are required in resolved state. Each step has unique `id`, title, and `completed`, `in_progress` or `pending` status. `steps: null` requires `summaryErrorLabel`; empty steps use supplied `emptyLabel` or “No steps”. No completion is inferred.
- Chat plan: two or more completed steps form a disclosure group. Remaining visible steps start at the first in-progress step, exclude completed steps, and are capped at five (`mobile: true`: three). `completedExpanded` supplies initial disclosure state. `completedCountLabel` and `showCompletedLabel` customize labels.
- `showPlanLabel` and `hidePlanLabel` together enable whole-plan collapse. `collapsed` supplies initial state. `layout: library` renders all steps in supplied order without disclosure. `planType: language_learning` numbers unfinished steps and omits whole-plan collapse. Initially collapsed library/learning layouts are rejected.

This is an explicitly supplied `mobile` mode, not an automatic viewport data-selection policy. CSS still adapts to narrow widths. Visual geometry is original; no native/pixel parity is claimed.

## Local actions

Real button activation supports native keyboard semantics. The following events bubble, are cancelable, non-composed, and contain frozen detail objects:

- `iui:automation-open`: `{id, automationId, url}`; `id` is the node ID or null, `automationId` is the item ID or null for the footer. There is no default navigation or remote effect.
- `iui:automation-toggle`: `{id, section, expanded}`, where section is `plan` or `completed`. Preventing default preserves current disclosure. Accepted events change local presentation only.

Controls honor supplied disabled state, current native/ARIA disabled state, disabled fieldsets including the first-legend exception, hidden/inert composed ancestry, event cancellation and permanent ownership retirement. A local admission gate blocks constructor reentry. Update/dispose during event construction or dispatch wins over stale work; ordinary errors remain observable. Form reset restores initial disclosure after cancellation and pending-reset reconciliation. Replacements reset local presentation to the newly supplied defaults.

## Integration and evidence

Domain installer: `installAutomationSchema({node,defs})` from `scripts/automation-schema.mjs`; registers the three nodes in the base schema group. Semantic validation: `inspectAutomation(node,path,add,isSafeURL)`. Renderer: `renderAutomation(context,node)`. Include `automation.css` in renderer embedded styles and the build's standalone stylesheet. The shared owner, generation, intent gate, painter and native-reset helpers are reused; no second resource registry exists.

Domain code is tested with temporary generator, core dispatch, renderer dispatch/style and build-CSS wiring. These shared-file changes are deliberately excluded from the domain-only commit and must be integrated serially before use. Generated schemas/declarations/validator are regenerated by the integrator. A domain-only commit by itself does not register or render a public node.

Tests cover resolved/pending/failed/empty data, validation, five-item list, chat/mobile/library/learning plan behavior, cancellation, reset, supplied disabled and fieldset gates, constructor reentry/error/update/dispose, stale ownership, compiled artifact behavior and replacement. `tests/browser/automation.spec.mjs` defines native Enter/Space, reset, cancellation, update/dispose and narrow-width checks; discovery alone is not execution. Native browser and pixel acceptance remain unverified until separately run.

Native reset anchors to the always-visible whole-plan header toggle when it
exists. The completed toggle inside a hidden plan body cannot veto that reset;
completed-only layouts continue to use their visible completed toggle.

## Source selection and precise validation

`automation/views` registers all three existing nodes from their single installer. `AUTOMATION_DATA` rejects whitespace-only strings on every top-level direct string field (including optional fallback and labels), every supplied item direct string field, viewAll label and each plan statusLabels value. Item URLs and viewAll URL must pass the safe link policy. Plan step titles must be nonblank; step/item IDs also have the schema's no-whitespace/control-character syntax. IDs must be unique within each item or step list, not across unrelated components.

Resolved `steps: null` requires summaryErrorLabel. Show/hide plan labels must be supplied as a pair. Initially collapsed plans require that pair and cannot use library layout or language_learning planType. These are supplied presentation consistency checks, not task scheduling or completion inference. Structural conditionals forbid active item/items/viewAll/steps as specified for unresolved states; other present strings and relationships still receive semantic validation. Run full `validateDocument`, not only the selected structural schema.
